text:
Mia Chen: quick summary — while doing a TP=2 end-to-end perf sweep on the new 8xA100 cluster, I hit a weird latency cliff when sequence length crossed ~1024. traces point at repeated small all-reduce ops blowing up tail latency. :frowning:

Raj Patel: can you paste the minimal repro command? also which NCCL version and our kernel-selection flags?

Mia Chen: repro command I used:
```bash
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 python perf/tp_run.py --model=llama-7b --tp=2 --batch=4 --seq=512,1024,2048 --warmup=20 --iters=50
```
NCCL 2.14.3, runtime kernel selection: default heuristics (seq-based kernel picker + weight-quant thresholds).

Sofia Gomez: interesting — when seq > 1024 we start chunking KV cache updates into much smaller fragments due to our current KV windowing. small fragments => many tiny all-reduces. ring algorithm has overhead for many small messages; tree reduces latency for many small messages (lower startup cost).

Mia Chen: here are a couple of profiler snippets (raw):
```
[tp_worker0] allreduce call #312 size=48KB latency=420us
[tp_worker1] allreduce call #313 size=48KB latency=430us
[tp_worker0] allreduce call #640 size=8KB latency=260us
[tp_worker1] allreduce call #641 size=8KB latency=270us
```
Notice the 8KB ops are much less efficient overall because we have 12x of them per forward step.

Alex Nguyen: :eyes: so there are two levers: 1) choose tree for sizes < ~16KB; 2) coalesce KV fragments to make fewer but larger all-reduces. which is less risky for rollout?

Raj Patel: kernel change is low-risk if we can gate by runtime profile (per-job switch). Coalescing requires touching chunking heuristics + correctness tests (more effort).

Sofia Gomez: also watch out for comm/compute overlap — our current dispatcher forces a barrier after KV sync which prevents overlapping later-stage matmul with inflight comms. If we relax that barrier and allow async allreduce with matching stream ops we get overlap and hide some cost. I ran a quick patch locally and saw 12% p50 improvement for seq=2048.

Mia Chen: sharing quick perf diff (before/after tree fallback + overlap):
```
seq=2048, batch=4: p50 before=210ms p95=342ms
seq=2048, batch=4: p50 after=183ms p95=255ms
```
P95 improved more with overlap + tree fallback.

Alex Nguyen: nice. Can you open a small RFC outlining: detection threshold, fallback policy, metrics to monitor (p50/p95 token latency, allreduce count, avg message size), and a canary plan? I'll sign off on a limited rollout.

Mia Chen: will do. one more data point: when we increased chunk alignment to 64KB instead of 16KB (so fewer fragments) throughput dropped slightly (2%) but latency improved substantially. that might be acceptable for latency-sensitive customers.

Raj Patel: add automated regression tests to perf harness: generate trace with lots of small KV ops and assert p95 < baseline * 1.1 for ring->tree fallback. Also add kernel-picker telemetry so we can see how often tree is chosen and correlate with P95.

perf-bot: new profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/profiles/2004512345 — includes nvtx trace and NCCL logs.

Sofia Gomez: thanks. action items: Mia to send RFC, Alex to review and propose rollout windows, Raj to add perf-tests and telemetry hooks. I'll prototype barrier-relax change and send a PR.

Mia Chen: target for RFC by EOD tomorrow. dropping initial notes into #perf-docs. :thumbsup:
